title.narrative: Greening Private Enterprises in Kosovo (GPEK) SDC
Grön omställning av privata företag i Kosovo (GPEK) SDC

description.narrative: Greening Private Enterprises in Kosovo (GPEK), implemented by SDC, aims to raise awareness among private companies on sustainability, support the adoption of greener technologies, and accelerate the green transition through a Challenge Fund that incentivizes investment and application of such solutions. The initiative offers clear opportunities for collaboration with Team Sweden actors.

Greening Private Enterprises in Kosovo (GPEK), som genomförs av SDC, syftar till att öka medvetenheten hos privata företag om hållbarhet, stödja införandet av grönare teknologier samt påskynda den gröna omställningen genom en Challenge Fund som stimulerar investeringar i och tillämpning av sådana lösningar. Initiativet erbjuder tydliga möjligheter till samverkan med aktörer inom Team Sweden.

Objective of the intervention The main objective of the GPEK is: "By the end of the intervention, small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Kosovo adopt environmentally sustainable business practices and innovative solutions that strengthen their competitiveness, reduce environmental impact, and contribute to inclusive green economic growth."
This objective is expected to be achieved through enhanced SME awareness of the business case for sustainability, strengthened local green service and finance ecosystems, and piloting of innovative SME-led solutions supported by a Challenge Fund. The project anticipates changes in SME behavior, improved market incentives for green practices, and increased availability of local support services and financial mechanisms, including linkages to the Kosovo Credit Guarantee Fund (KCGF) for green financing.
At the impact level, the primary beneficiaries are Kosovo's small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), which account for more than 99% of all registered private-sector firms. SMEs form the backbone of the country's economy and play a critical role in competitiveness, employment generation, and innovation.
Theory of change: the projects theory of change follows a market systems development (MSD) approach.
1. Inform - Improved awareness for green transition SMEs gain awareness and practical knowledge of the benefits of adopting green practices.
2. Enable - Improved enabling environment for green growth Local market actors, including service providers, financial institutions, and public bodies, are strengthened to support SME transition to green solutions.
3. Transform - Strengthened green innovation ecosystem and challenge fund Early adopters and Challenge Fund beneficiaries demonstrate viable green business models that trigger wider market uptake and systemic change.
If Kosovo's SMEs have greater awareness of green opportunities, practical knowledge of EU requirements and market standards, supported by engaged public institutions and informed consumers (INFORM) AND have access to sustainable business services, tailored green financial instruments, and enabling policies that reduce the cost and risk of green investment (ENABLE) AND if pioneering SMEs and value chains pilot and demonstrate viable green business models and technologies that deliver both commercial and environmental benefits (TRANSFORM) THEN SMEs will increasingly adopt market-driven green innovations and practices that lower costs and improve competitiveness thereby generating new and/or better jobs and improving environmental performance.
Together; inform, enable and transform lead to the project's overall impact Enhancing the competitiveness and resilience of Kosovo's SMEs by supporting their transition toward cleaner and more resource-efficient technologies and practices, generating new and/or better jobs and improving environmental performance.
Impact indicators and targets 1) Number of persons in new and/or better jobs created through private enterprise greening and innovation. Baseline (2026): 0 persons in new and/or better green jobs. Target (2031): 1,500 persons in new and/or better green jobs (40% new 60% better).
2) Total value of private sector capital mobilized through project support activities. Baseline (2026): 0 € private sector capital mobilized. Target (2031): €15 million private sector capital mobilized.
3) Number of private enterprises reporting improved resource efficiency, productivity, and/or expanded access to regional/EU markets due to adoption of green practices supported by the project. Baseline (2026): 0 private enterprises with improved resource efficiency, productivity, and/or expanded market access. Target (2031): 110 private enterprises with improved resource efficiency, productivity, and/or expanded market access.
